question: Should OpenClaw adopt `gateway.readiness` plus the public `registerReadinessCriterion` plugin API as a supported core contract after the prerequisite framework is accepted?
rationale: This is not a narrow bug repair: it defines durable operator configuration, externally consumable plugin API behavior, and opt-in availability semantics. Code review alone cannot choose whether those permanent product contracts belong in core.

options.title: Sponsor the readiness contract
options.body: Approve the configuration and plugin SDK direction, then require exact-head live proof for legacy and selected-criterion modes before merge.

options.title: Keep the framework generic
options.body: Do not add the owner criteria or plugin API until a narrower maintainer-approved API contract and support boundary are defined.

options.title: Pause the follow-on stack
options.body: Hold this branch until the prerequisite framework has merged and current-main integration can be reviewed as a single coherent contract.

recommendation.title: Sponsor the readiness contract
recommendation.body: Approve the configuration and plugin SDK direction, then require exact-head live proof for legacy and selected-criterion modes before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: This author owns the submitted readiness proposal and prerequisite stack, though a repository decision-maker must sponsor the permanent API direction.
